feature: Finishing a title and picking a dissolve land inside 50 ms
summary: Command Return on a typed title over a video and a click on the Cross dissolve tile at a cut now each hold the window under 50 ms, so neither drops a frame you can feel. The picture changes in the click's frame; the timeline, the panel and the menu bar catch up in the next.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default.

try.do: Open the sample recording and click Edit.
Click the join between two pieces of the recording on V1, then click Cross dissolve in the picker.
Press T, click on the picture and type a title.
Watch the timeline as the title lands: its Title track comes in a frame after the words.
Right after either step, open the Edit menu and check Undo names what you just did.

evaluate: Does Command Return on a title now feel instant?
Does the Cross dissolve tile answer the moment you click it?
Does anything flicker as the Title track, the panel's sections and the title's effects arrive one after another?
Is the menu bar ever out of date when you reach for it right after an edit?
rough: Before and after, an-editing-session-walk, three runs in a row each: longest pass after Command Return 55-64 ms before, 42.5 / 43.7 / 43.9 ms after; Cross dissolve tile 50-63 ms before, 34.9 / 36.3 / 40.7 ms after. The walk's two claims are now 50 ms.

The worst pass left after Command Return is no longer the commit (now 32-45 ms) but a title's effect panes arriving about 350 ms later, each followed by SwiftUI's accessibility pass over the new controls. It has the least margin of the three.
The menu bar now follows every document edit a frame late on Next (as it already followed the playhead), so for one frame after an edit a menu row's dimming can be one edit behind.
Picking a dissolve tile now picks the cut and moves the playhead one frame after the cut wears the transition, so the panel's form for the cut lands a frame after the click.

The tile's own pass still carries about 35 ms that no single view owns: SwiftUI's whole-window update, layout and accessibility focus after any change at all. Closing the picker without changing anything costs nearly as much as the full pick.
